{{Quote|'''FIFTH REMINDER''': Please return your EV to your MerenData dealer for double your money back. We are also offering a 10,000-credit reward for information leading to the whereabouts of other EV supervisor droids.|MerenData customer mailing|<ref name="TNEGtD" />}}
The '''EV-series supervisor droid''' was a model of [[Supervisor droid/Legends|supervisor droid]] manufactured by [[MerenData/Legends|MerenData]]. Originally designed to be an efficient taskmaster for automated labor pools, the series suffered from a number of unfortunate "glitches" and was one of the largest corporate disasters in [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|history]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:EVSupDroid_egtd.png|thumb|left|180px|The schematics of an EV-series supervisor droid]]
The EV-series was a model of [[Supervisor droid/Legends|supervisor droid]] with a rod-thin build and a grating mechanical voice. [[Color/Legends|Bronze]]-colored [[Droid/Legends|droids]]<ref name="EV-9D9" /> with polished [[Plastron/Legends|plastron]] plating,<ref name="TCVD" /> they were equipped with a [[Heuristic processor/Legends|heuristic processor]]<ref name="SGtD" /> and an advanced [[Personality matrix/Legends|personality matrix]].<ref name="CFTD" /> In addition to [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and [[Binary/Legends|binary]], a new EV could speak 3 unassigned [[Language/Legends|languages]].<ref name="SGtD" /> Their heads featured an [[Audio sensor/Legends|auditory receptor]], a [[Broadband antenna/Legends|broadband broadcast antenna/receiver system]],<ref name="CFTD" /> its logic center, a pair of<ref name="CE" /> golden<ref name="TNR" /> [[Human/Legends|Human]]-range<ref name="CFTD" /> [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]],<ref name="CE" /> and a speech mimic flap<ref name="TCVD" /> synchronized<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> with its [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]]. An EV also had an internal<ref name="SGtD" /> high-frequency binary [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]<ref name="TNEGtD" /> and its cervical servomotor was located in its chest. Their power axis contained a recharge coupling access port and was attached to the droid's pelvic mount, which could lock into [[Limb/Legends|legs]] or a motorized cart.<ref name="TCVD" /> When equipped with legs, they stood 1.9 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall. They also had a pair of manipulator arms<ref name="CE" /> tipped with hand appendages.<ref name="SGtD" />

During production, the standard [[EV motivator]]<ref name="TNEGtD" /> originally planned for the EV was accidentally swapped<ref name="SGtD" /> with the [[MDF motivator]], a contraband piece of hardware designed for use in [[Interrogation droid/Legends|torture droids]].<ref name="TNEGtD" /> While the droids with the swapped [[Motivator/Legends|motivators]] actually outperformed the unaltered droids when it came to managing the droids under their care<ref name="SGtD" /> and worker motivation,<ref name="TNEGtD" /> they used sadistic methods to accomplish their tasks.<ref name="SGtD" />

EV-series supervisor droids could be modified to perform different functions. Many military units swore by the use of an EV unit as a quartermaster for supplies thanks to its meticulous skill at keeping supplies protected and in good working condition. This relativity simple modification process was started by installing a video recorder the droid could use to keep a visual catalog of supplies and to track missing items. A power charger was then installed in the droid's torso so it could keep [[Power cell/Legends|power packs]] fully charged. Finally, the EV was given a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] with access to the military unit's inventory.

[[File:WickedAndEvil.png|thumb|right|250px|An EV-series droid [[Battle of Endor/Legends|battles]] the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket]].]]
They could also be used as [[Technician/Legends|technicians]]. Although this modification may have seemed unlikely for a supervisor droid, EV units had a working knowledge of how machines functioned and could be quite adept at fixing them. This modification emphasized the droid's ability to make repairs and adjustments to machines and other droids or [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] beings. It included removing the EV unit's internal comlink and, in its place, installing a [[Diagnostic scanner/Legends|diagnostics package]] to help it find and fix problems. It also entailed equipping the droid with a tool kit and a roll of [[mesh tape]] for emergency repairs. Optionally, one of the EV unit's hand appendages could be swapped out for a tool appendage with a multifunction apparatus, giving it the ability to connect up to three tools needed to perform a particular job. Finally, a [[targeting scope]] was added to the droid's head and calibrated, which required 15 [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] of work.<ref name="SGtD" />

==History==
{{Quote|I have seen much damage, heard many complaints from droids about working under EV-Series. Scarred chassis, broken and severed arms and legs, burned hardware&mdash;just some of the carnage I have seen on poor droids that come to me for repairs.|[[Klikk]]|<ref name="SGtD" />}}
Whether through negligence or sabotage, an employee substituted a case of MDF motivators intended for use in torture droids for the standard EV motivator during the production of the EV-series supervisor droid.<ref name="TNEGtD" /> Only noticing the error after several shipments of the faulty droids,<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> hundreds of individual units,<ref name="TNEGtD" /> had already gone out,<ref name="AIR" /> MerenData chose not to take immediate action, as torture droids were highly illegal and the company was not supposed to have access to MDF motivators in the first place.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

For the first few [[Standard month/Legends|months]] following the EV's release to market, MerenData instead adopted a wait-and-see approach<ref name="TNEGtD" /> to see how the droids performed.<ref name="SGtD" /> Various industry surveys<ref name="AIR" /> indicated that MDF-equipped EV units were actually outperforming those equipped with the intended motivators when it came to worker motivation.<ref name="TNEGtD" /> However, when complaints began arriving at the company's offices<ref name="FF17">{{FactFile|17|SUP 1-2|EV-9D9 Supervisor Droid}}</ref> regarding the sadistic methods they used to accomplish their tasks,<ref name="SGtD" /> it was exposed that MerenData was building illegal droids for the [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]]. Despite blaming the mix-up on industrial sabotage, MerenData had a public relations nightmare on its hands.<ref name="TNEGtD" /> Faced with a massive lawsuit,<ref name="TNEGtD" /> MerenData was forced to recall the model to exchange motivators. While most of the droids were returned to the company and repaired, some customers preferred the flawed model,<ref name="SGtD" /> leading MerenData to begin offering incentives for returns and reports on the whereabouts of other EV units.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

Following the recall, MerenData introduced several replacement models,<ref name="TNEGtD" /> including the second-generation [[EV-II]], which compensated for the personality flaws of its predecessor,<ref name="CFTD" /> and the [[V-series droid supervisor/Legends|V-series droid supervisor]],<ref name="TCVD" /> a relaunch of the EV-series marketed towards the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]].<ref name="TNEGtD" /> Ironically, without the infamous MDF motivators of the first-generation EVs, both models were considered unimpressive performers.<ref name="TNEGtD" /> Both lines were financial failures, forcing MerenData to close thousands of branch offices from the [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TNEGtD" />

[[File:NS_service_droid.png|thumb|right|250px|A EV-series serving the Nightsisters.]]
[[Ploovo Two-For-One/Legends|Ploovo Two-For-One]] employed an original EV series droid,<ref name="AIR" /> as did crime lord [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. The [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] owned a droid model with the head of which somewhat resembled the one of the EV-series supervisor droid. Around [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]], such droids were seen serving drinks to [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Zalem/Legends|Zalem]] and her fellow [[Sister (Witches of Dathomir)|Sisters]] under a [[Tent/Legends|tent]].<ref name="IE3">[[Star Wars (1998) 25|''Star Wars'' (1998) 25]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Unlike most sources, which identify the EV-series supervisor/interrogator droid as a third-degree droid, the ''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]'' labels it a fourth-degree droid.<ref name="AEG">''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''</ref>
